newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to put some coal mines in trust management.
newsitem.headline: Russia to put some coal mines in trust management.

text.p: The Russian government plans to organise auctions to put some coal mines in trust management soon, a government official said on Thursday.

The State Property Committee and OAO Rossiisky Ugolnaya Kompaniya (Rossugol) sent the government a list of mines to be put into trust on Wednesday, Rossugol President Yuri Malyshev told a news conference.
According to an agreement with the World Bank, Russia must put mines, accounting for 65 million tonnes of annual production out of a total of 260 million tonnes, in trust, he said.
The government will put more than the required number of mines into trust though Russia does not have laws on trust management, he said.
The Russian government is currently in talks with the World Bank on the second half of a $500 million credit to the coal industry, where about 400,000 miners have been on strike since Tuesday.
Malyshev said he expected the deal to be signed on December 10.

The trust management system has been widely used in neighbouring Kazakhstan, where the government has organised tenders to find outside managers for large enterprises rather than privatising them directly.
